prompt:
Tools that declare no kind are treated as read-only

Every tool has a `kind` (read, meta, edit, exec). It drives scheduling (consecutive read/meta calls run in parallel) and permissions (plan mode refuses edit/exec). We are about to accept tools from outside sources (MCP) that may not declare a kind at all, and today such a tool gets the most permissive handling:

- if the model calls two kind-less tools in one turn, they run concurrently in the parallel read-only batch;
- in plan mode the call is not refused, and the tool actually runs.

Repro: register a tool object with name, description, schema, summarize, subject and run but no `kind`, put the agent in plan mode, and have the model call it. It executes.

Expected: a tool that declares no kind gets the strictest handling, exactly like an `exec` tool. It runs one call at a time, never overlapping with another call, and results stay in call order. In plan mode it is refused without running, and its tool result is the standard plan-mode refusal text (PLAN_MODE_REASON), the same as for any shell command. `kind` should also be optional on the Tool type so such tools type-check.

Add or update tests as appropriate.
